title: Martin Roman, Freddy Johnson, Hawkins and Princess Beatrix's birth
summary: He recalls Martin Roman and Freddy Johnson in a concentration camp, Coleman Hawkins in Holland in 1938, and hearing "A Foggy Day" the day Beatrix was born.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I met a piano player named Martin Roman. He was from Germany. He was Jewish. He was the piano player with a band called Adde(?) Roselander(?). He would support Louis Armstrong.... A bunch of good musicians... I never saw him again. But Martin Roman spent time in a concentration camp with Freddy Johnson; both of them were in there together.
Where did they do that? In Holland or where?

In Holland. Come to think about it, I remember in Holland in 1938 Coleman Hawkins was playing at the (?) Palace with Freddy Johnson. I heard from...what, 125 miles from Rotterdam to Amsterdam. That was on the

date, the very day that Princess Beatrix was born. They had... Oh, the whole country went wild about it. I have trinkets that I picked up from around then, you know, to (?) about that. Oh, the country was (?). I took snapshots of Vollendam(?). No way did I stop. And on that very day I saw a picture called Damsels In Distress, with Fred Astaire, I think... Who was that English composer and trumpet player who wrote "Life is a..." [PAUSE] "Love is a splendid thing, dah-da-dah-de..." Who was he? Anyway, he was in that picture. And "A Foggy Day In London Town"; that was the first time I heard that song -- in Holland.
I wonder who that could be.
English. He wrote a beautiful song there.
Composer, yeah. And bandleader. He went to Holland.
